note: Attacker-controlled input bytes are written to a temporary file that will be passed to upx_main with -t (test) flag.
The fuzzer invokes upx_main with argv = {upx, -t, infilename}, setting opt->cmd to CMD_TEST.
PackMaster is constructed with the input file and options; test() is called for CMD_TEST.
getUnpacker identifies the file as a packed ELF64 and creates a PackLinuxElf64 object; doTest() is invoked.
doTest calls unpack() which performs the decompression and restoration of the packed ELF64.
The member MemBuffer ibuf is allocated with blocksize+OVERHEAD bytes; this buffer will later hold the PT_DYNAMIC segment.
un_DT_INIT is called with the PT_DYNAMIC program header (dynhdr) from the uncompressed ELF header.
The size of the PT_DYNAMIC segment is read from the program header; this value is attacker-controlled via the packed file.
The file offset of the PT_DYNAMIC segment is read from the program header; also attacker-controlled.
dyn_len bytes are read from file offset dyn_off into the member buffer ibuf. If dyn_len exceeds the allocated ibuf size, this overflows the heap buffer.
dynseg is set to point into ibuf, which now contains the attacker-controlled PT_DYNAMIC entries.
invert_pt_dynamic is called with dynseg pointing into ibuf and a length derived from attacker-controlled dyn_len.
Scans dynseg for DT_GNU_HASH tag; the tag value and the number of entries are fully attacker-controlled.
elf_find_dynamic returns a pointer computed from the attacker-controlled DT_GNU_HASH value added to file_image.
elf_find_table_size is called with the attacker-controlled DT_GNU_HASH tag; it will index dynseg using the hash table header values.

x_ndx is derived from attacker-controlled fields in the GNU hash table header (n_buckets, symoffset, bloom_size). The expression dynseg[-1+x_ndx] reads beyond the allocated ibuf heap buffer, causing a heap-use-after-free / out-of-bounds read when x_ndx is large.
